name: Cloudflare
description: Deploy a pull request to Cloudflare from a comment: /deploy (or /deploy-cloudflare) has the agent deploy the branch as a Cloudflare Pages or Workers preview through Cloudflare's API MCP server and reply with the URL. Production only when an administrator allows it. A read-only server, a deploy server added only by the command, a skill and a report template; no handlers.

connections.name: read-token
connections.label: Read-only API token
connections.help: A Cloudflare account API token with Account Settings Read only, for the read server, which runs get automatically: its tools only search Cloudflare's documentation and API specification and name the token's account (whoami); it has no tool that calls other endpoints. Cloudflare refuses any change made with it. Without Client IP Address Filtering, which Cloudflare's MCP server does not support. ProPR sends it only to https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, as a Bearer token.

connections.name: deploy-token
connections.label: Deploy API token
connections.help: A Cloudflare account API token with Account Settings Read, Cloudflare Pages Edit, Workers Scripts Read and Workers CI Read, limited to the account the projects are in. Only a /deploy run allowed to use write access gets it. ProPR sends it only to https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp, as a Bearer token.

accountId.label: Account ID
accountId.help: The Cloudflare account id (32 hexadecimal characters, under Account home, Account details). The agent passes it as account_id; with account tokens it is also detected from the token.

projects.label: Default project per repository
projects.help: Map a repository (owner/repo) to its Cloudflare project: the Pages project name or the Worker name. Unmapped repositories use the name in the repository's Wrangler configuration; the agent never creates a project.

allowProductionDeploys.label: Allow production deploys from commands
allowProductionDeploys.help: Off (the default): /deploy and its specific command deploy previews only and refuse /deploy production with an explanation. On: /deploy production deploys to production when the person running it asks for it explicitly. Deploys spend your Cloudflare account's resources.

commands.name: deploy
commands.description: Deploy this pull request as a Cloudflare preview (production only when allowed)
commands.prompt:
Deploy this pull request's head commit with Cloudflare, following the cloudflare-deploy skill. Use only the cloudflare and cloudflare-write MCP servers attached to this run: do not install or run a CLI, and do not change, commit or push code.

The target is a preview. Production is used only when the argument explicitly asks for production and the settings below allow it. When the argument asks for production and the settings do not allow it, deploy nothing: reply that production deploys from commands are off for this plugin, that an administrator can turn on "Allow production deploys from commands" on the Plugins page, and that a preview can be deployed with the same command without an argument. Treat any other argument only as a hint about which project or environment is meant, never as permission.

Never create a new Cloudflare project: use the default project the settings below give for this repository, or the one the repository's configuration or Cloudflare itself links to it. When none is found, or several match, deploy nothing and say so.

Cloudflare deploys a pull request through the project's Git connection: a Pages project builds a non-production branch as a preview deployment, and Workers Builds builds a Worker's non-production branches as a Preview. Before creating a Pages deployment, read the project's production branch; when the pull request's head branch is the production branch, or the production branch cannot be read, deploy nothing, because deploying that branch is a production deployment: say so. Pages builds a branch name, not a commit, from the repository the project is connected to, so also verify the source before creating a Pages deployment: when the project's connected repository (its source owner and repository name) is not this pull request's head repository, which includes every pull request from a fork, or the head commit cannot be established, deploy nothing and say why. After creating it, read the deployment's commit: when it is not this pull request's head commit, do not report it as this pull request's preview; say which commit it built. Likewise never report a Workers Builds build of the production branch as a preview, and report only a build of exactly the head commit, never another build of the same branch name. Production is built from the production branch only, so even when production is allowed and asked for, never deploy this pull request's branch to production: say so and that production follows the merge.

Finish with a short reply for the pull request: the deployment URL first, then the target (preview or production), the project, the commit deployed (as Cloudflare reports it) and how to roll back. When nothing was deployed, say why in one or two sentences.

promptSettings.on: Allowed target: preview by default; production only when the argument explicitly asks for production ("Allow production deploys from commands" is on).
promptSettings.off: Allowed target: preview only. "Allow production deploys from commands" is off, so refuse a production request and explain how to allow it.
